source_review_notes: Main references continue on page 31 above Appendix A. Header-only location is distinct from appendix content review; no B1-B4 bodies were read.
Theorem 1(ii), (3.23), and Theorem 2(ii), (3.28), print equalities without explicit limit signs under an asymptotic introductory sentence. Preserve them; do not silently replace by limits.
Theorem 2 lists B1-B4 and C1-C2, not the immediately preceding C3. Parts (ii) and (iii) explicitly say under (3.7), despite the opening under (3.7) and (3.9).
Theorem 3 lists B1-B4 and C2, not C1. Its alternative condition uses min(p1,m), while its distributional limits use min(p1,p2,m).
The main-text B1-B4 reference is on page 7, before Lemma 1. The appendix extension of B1(ii) is mentioned on page 16 in a distinct extension discussion, not a full definition of B1.
The source rate l_(p1,p2,m) has denominator sqrt(m p2), confirmed in a magnified PDF crop, not sqrt(m) times p2. Its logarithmic multiplier is (ln^2 p1 ln p2 ln m)^(1+epsilon).

The source almost-sure O notation is defined by convergence of a ratio to a finite constant, rather than the usual eventual boundedness; Omega likewise uses a positive limit. Preserve these nonstandard conventions.

The initial column estimator uses leading eigenvectors of M_r=(T p1)^(-1) sum_(t=1)^T X_t transpose X_t in the printed formula. Do not silently replace the full-T expression by training length m. Online source availability needs explicit scope notes.
Equation (1.2) describes zero/one-way factor cases, although page 8 references (1.2) as the null of no changepoint. Record this mismatched reference while retaining the explicit no-break prose.

The randomization is y_tau=z_tau+psi_tau with iid standard normal z_tau. P* conditions on the observed whole data array; theorems hold for almost all array realizations. Do not identify y_tau as exactly centered iid normal at finite sample when psi_tau is nonzero.
The trace normalization in (3.15) includes 1/p1 times the sum of all eigenvalues. Its denominator is not just the unscaled trace.

Partial-sum trimming r_Tm tends to infinity and r_Tm/Tm tends to zero. The Wiener process is named on page 12; the standard Brownian convention is ambient, with the ratio at u=0 requiring its limiting interpretation.

Partial-sum normalizers are alpha=sqrt(2 ln ln Tm), beta=2 ln ln Tm+(1/2)ln ln ln Tm-(1/2)ln pi. Maximum normalizers are a=b/(1+b^2), b=sqrt(2 ln Tm)-(ln ln Tm+ln(4pi))/(2 sqrt(2 ln Tm)). These families are distinct.
The no-break-training condition concerns the column space of R, while R is the row-factor loading matrix. C2 specifies diverging monitoring length and Omega(m^varsigma), varsigma>=1.

The additional Section 4 decreasing-factor and time-varying-C discussions are not extra Theorems. Their formulas and possible source inconsistencies should not be imported into the three original theorem claims.
